mn144:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary.
mn144:2.1: Now on that occasion the venerable Sāriputta, the venerable Mahā Cunda, and the venerable Channa were living on the mountain Vulture Peak.
mn144:3.1: On that occasion the venerable Channa was afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill.
mn144:3.2: Then, when it was evening, the venerable Sāriputta rose from meditation, went to the venerable Mahā Cunda, and said to him:
mn144:3.3: “Friend Cunda, let us go to the venerable Channa and ask about his illness.”
mn144:3.4: “Yes, friend,” the venerable Mahā Cunda replied.
mn144:4.1: Then the venerable Sāriputta and the venerable Mahā Cunda went to the venerable Channa and exchanged greetings with him.
mn144:4.2: When this courteous and amiable talk was finished, they sat down at one side and the venerable Sāriputta said to the venerable Channa:
mn144:4.3: “I hope you are getting well, friend Channa, I hope you are comfortable. I hope your painful feelings are subsiding and not increasing, and that their subsiding, not their increase, is apparent.”
mn144:5.1: “Friend Sāriputta, I am not getting well, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase and not their subsiding is apparent.
mn144:5.2: Just as if a strong man were splitting my head open with a sharp sword, so too, violent winds cut through my head.
mn144:5.3: I am not getting well, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase and not their subsiding is apparent.
mn144:5.4: Just as if a strong man were tightening a tough leather strap around my head as a headband, so too, there are violent pains in my head.
mn144:5.5: I am not getting well, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase and not their subsiding is apparent.
mn144:5.6: Just as if a skilled butcher or his apprentice were to carve up an ox’s belly with a sharp butcher’s knife, so too, violent winds are carving up my belly.
mn144:5.7: I am not getting well, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase and not their subsiding is apparent.
mn144:5.8: Just as if two strong men were to seize a weaker man by both arms and roast him over a pit of hot coals, so too, there is a violent burning in my body.
mn144:5.9: I am not getting well, I am not comfortable. My painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase and not their subsiding is apparent.
mn144:5.10: I shall use the knife, friend Sāriputta; I have no desire to live.”
mn144:6.1: “Let the venerable Channa not use the knife.
mn144:6.2: Let the venerable Channa live. We want the venerable Channa to live.
mn144:6.3: If he lacks suitable food, I will go in search of suitable food for him.
mn144:6.4: If he lacks suitable medicine, I will go in search of suitable medicine for him.
mn144:6.5: If he lacks a proper attendant, I will attend on him.
mn144:6.6: Let the venerable Channa not use the knife.
mn144:6.7: Let the venerable Channa live. We want the venerable Channa to live.”
mn144:7.1: “Friend Sāriputta, it is not that I have no suitable food;
mn144:7.2: it is not that I have no suitable medicine;
mn144:7.3: it is not that I have no proper attendant.
mn144:7.4: But rather, friend Sāriputta, the Teacher has long been worshipped by me with love, not without love;
mn144:7.5: for it is proper for the disciple to worship the Teacher with love, not without love.
mn144:7.6: Friend Sāriputta, remember this: ‘the bhikkhu Channa will use the knife blamelessly.’”
mn144:8.1: “We would ask the venerable Channa certain questions, if the venerable Channa finds it opportune to reply.”
mn144:8.2: “Ask, friend Sāriputta. When I have heard, I shall know.”
mn144:9.1: “Friend Channa, do you regard the eye, eye-consciousness, and things cognizable [by the mind] through eye-consciousness thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?
mn144:9.2: Do you regard the ear, ear-consciousness…
mn144:9.6: the mind, mind-consciousness, and things cognizable [by the mind] through mind-consciousness thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”
mn144:9.7: “Friend Sāriputta, I regard the eye, eye-consciousness, and things cognizable [by the mind] through eye-consciousness thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’.
mn144:9.12: the mind, mind-consciousness, and things cognizable [by the mind] through mind-consciousness thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’.”
mn144:10.1: “Friend Channa, what have you seen and directly known in the eye, in eye-consciousness, and in things cognizable [by the mind] through eye-consciousness, that you regard them thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’?
mn144:10.2: What have you seen and directly known in the ear, in ear-consciousness…
mn144:10.6: in the mind, in mind-consciousness, and in things cognizable [by the mind] through mind-consciousness, that you regard them thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’?”
mn144:10.7: “Friend Sāriputta, it is through seeing and directly knowing cessation in the eye, in eye-consciousness, and in things cognizable [by the mind] through eye-consciousness, that I regard them thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’.
mn144:10.8: It is through seeing and directly knowing cessation in the ear, in ear-consciousness…
mn144:10.12: in the mind, in mind-consciousness, and in things cognizable [by the mind] through mind-consciousness, that I regard them thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self’.”
mn144:11.1: When this was said, the venerable Mahā Cunda said to the venerable Channa:
mn144:11.2: “Therefore, friend Channa, this instruction of the Blessed One’s is to be constantly given attention:
mn144:11.3: ‘There is wavering in one who is dependent, there is no wavering in one who is independent;
mn144:11.4: when there is no wavering, there is tranquillity;
mn144:11.5: when there is tranquillity, there is no bias;
mn144:11.6: when there is no bias, there is no coming and going;
mn144:11.7: when there is no coming and going, there is no passing away and reappearing;
mn144:11.8: when there is no passing away and reappearing, there is no here nor beyond nor in between.
mn144:11.9: This is the end of suffering.’”
mn144:11.10: Then when the venerable Sāriputta and the venerable Mahā Cunda had advised the venerable Channa thus, they rose from their seats and went away.
mn144:12.1: Then, soon after the venerable Sāriputta and the venerable Mahā Cunda had gone, the venerable Channa used the knife.
mn144:13.1: Then the venerable Sāriputta went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he sat down at one side and said to the Blessed One:
mn144:13.2: “Venerable sir, the venerable Channa has used the knife.
mn144:13.3: What is his destination, what is his future course?”
mn144:13.4: “Sāriputta, didn’t the bhikkhu Channa declare to you his blamelessness?”
mn144:13.5: “Venerable sir, there is a Vajjian village called Pubbajira.
mn144:13.6: There the venerable Channa had friendly families, intimate families, approachable families [as his supporters].”
mn144:13.7: “Indeed, Sāriputta, the bhikkhu Channa had friendly families, intimate families, approachable families [as his supporters];
mn144:13.8: but I do not say that to this extent he was blameworthy.
mn144:13.9: Sāriputta, when one lays down this body and takes up a new body, then I say one is blameworthy.
mn144:13.10: This did not happen in the case of the bhikkhu Channa;
mn144:13.11: remember this, Sāriputta: ‘the bhikkhu Channa used the knife blamelessly.’”
mn144:13.12: That is what the Blessed One said.
mn144:13.13: The venerable Sāriputta was satisfied and delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
